{{Quote|Welcome aboard! This is Captain Rex from the cockpit. I know this is probably your first flight, and it's&hellip; mine too.|RX-24|<ref name="ST" />}}
'''RX-24''', nicknamed '''Rex''', was an [[RX-series pilot droid/Legends|RX-series pilot droid]] manufactured by [[Reubens Robotic Systems]]. The [[Gender/Legends|masculine]]-[[Programmer/Legends|programmed]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]] was purchased by the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] travel agency at some point after the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and prior to 1 BBY, but he was defective as of [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]] and saw no service until after the company upgraded its fleet of [[StarSpeeder 1000]] [[Starship/Legends|spacecraft]] to the newer [[StarSpeeder 3000]] [[Time/Legends|sometime]] around the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. By that time, RX-24 had been repaired, and the company placed him into service. His initial duty to Star Tours constituted multiple firsts: Rex's first flight as a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], the first official Star Tours use of the StarSpeeder 3000 [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]], and the first outing of the [[Endor Express]] with non-stop service to the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor]]. With the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] as his copilot, Rex took off on [[Star Tours Flight 45]]. He never reached Endor. Instead, Rex nearly crashed the shuttle leaving the [[Tomorrowland Starport|spaceport]], emerged from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] too late and overshot the Forest [[Moon/Legends|Moon]], stumbled into a [[Comet/Legends|comet]] field, wandered into a [[Battle of Death Star III|battle]] between [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and Imperial forces, and joined an attack run on an Imperial [[Death Star III|battlestation]]. The [[Pilot droid/Legends|pilot droid]] then returned to the spaceport from which the flight originated.

Rex's programming and appearance were standard for the RX series. He had a segmented body with wider sections of burnished metal trimmed in [[Color/Legends|gold]] and purple, and narrower sections in black. He had three [[Limb/Legends|arms]] with clawed hands, blue [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] that glowed with a white light, a retractable purple visor, and a [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] generator at his base to facilitate movement. Rex was friendly with organic beings, and he affected a brave demeanor even during his disastrous flight to Endor. Fellow droid [[ROX-N]] was known to have romantic feelings toward Rex.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Okay! I've always wanted to do this. We're going in!|RX-24, joining Red Squadron in an attack run on an Imperial battlestation|<ref name="ST" />}}
[[File:Defective_RX-24_SWI127.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Upon arrival at Star Tours from the factory, RX-24 was marked as defective.]]
RX-24 was an [[RX-series pilot droid/Legends|RX-series pilot droid]] manufactured by [[Reubens Robotic Systems]].<ref name="CSWE III 117" /> The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] was one of several purchased by the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] travel agency known as [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] circa [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]].<ref name="ST2 date">{{SW|url=news/convenient-daily-departures-the-history-of-star-tours|text=Convenient Daily Departures: The History of ''Star Tours''|int=Convenient Daily Departures: The History of Star Tours|nolive=1}}</ref> RX-24 was shipped to the agency defective; once removed from his shipping crate, the droid was almost completely non-functional, muttering random phrases in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], speeding up and slowing down his speech at irregular intervals, and sparking at the neck. With a decal reading, "<small>DEFECTIVE</small>" and "<small>RETURN TO FACTORY</small>" on his base, he sat outside his crate up to the [[Time/Legends|time]] of [[Star Tours Flight 1401]],<ref name="ST2" /> which took place at some point between [[2 BBY/Legends|2]] and 0 BBY. Nevertheless, Star Tours decided to keep RX-24 at the company and had its in-house repair droids restore him to working order.<ref name="ST2 date" />

By [[4 ABY/Legends|4.3 ABY]],<ref name="LC blog">{{Blog|holocron|7|Death Star timeline}}</ref> shortly after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> RX-24 had been brought online as a fully functional [[Pilot droid/Legends|pilot droid]].<ref name="ST" /> He also struck up a romantic relationship with another Star Tours droid, [[ROX-N]].<ref name="SWI104">{{InsiderCite|104|Star Tours: Taking Off on a Star Tour|''Star Tours'': Taking Off on a Star Tour}}</ref> Star Tours had upgraded its fleet of [[StarSpeeder 1000]] passenger [[Starship/Legends|starships]]<ref name="ST2" /> to the newer [[StarSpeeder 3000]] model.<ref name="CSWE III 117" /> Seeking to cash in on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Endor (planet)/Legends|Endor's]] sudden fame<ref name="CSWE III 189b">{{CSWECite|III|189|Star Tours Travel Agency}}</ref> after the defeat of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] there,<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Star Tours assigned RX-24, now nicknamed "Rex," to [[Captain/Legends|captain]] the StarSpeeder 3000 on its maiden voyage,<ref name="CSWE III 189b" /> taking it to the [[Tree/Legends|forest]] moon with a full complement of passengers as part of the newly implemented [[Endor Express]] service.<ref name="ST" /> Rex was to follow the [[Sanctuary Pipeline/Legends|Sanctuary Pipeline]], a [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]]<ref name="CSWE III 189b" /> that had been created by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] to bring supplies to the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]] during the construction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. Without the Empire to maintain the hyperroute, however, the Pipeline began to decay soon after the battle had ended.<ref name="G9">{{GamerCite|9|Endor and the Moddell Sector}}</ref> Nevertheless, Star Tours gave the go-ahead for Rex to [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Star Tours Flight 45]] (ST-45).<ref name="CSWE III 189a">{{CSWECite|III|189|Starspeeder 3000}}</ref> Only the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], temporarily working for the travel agency, saw the folly of the plan, noting that Rex still had his "Remove Before Flight" factory tag on him.<ref name="SWI104" />

[[File:Startours_DSIII.jpg|thumb|right|upright|250px|Rex's first flight brought him to an immense Imperial battlestation.]]
Rex took his post in front of the StarSpeeder's [[cockpit shield]]. Promising a smooth ride, the droid lowered the shield and greeted his passengers as his [[Navigator/Legends|navigator]], [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], was loaded into the craft's [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech]] [[Astromech socket/Legends|slot]]. With approval from control, Rex lurched the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] into motion but then took a wrong turn while still inside the Star Tours spaceport. Unable to find the StarSpeeder 3000's brakes, he nearly collided with a wall before wrenching the craft up and over the obstruction and into [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Despite this inauspicious beginning, RX-24 then ordered R2-D2 to launch the craft into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]].<ref name="ST" />

The pilot's next mistake was to come out of [[Lightspeed/Legends|lightspeed]] too late, passing [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] completely and inadvertently moving the StarSpeeder into a field of [[Water/Legends|icy]] [[Comet/Legends|comets]] instead. He deftly piloted the craft through the comet field only to emerge within a restricted combat zone, where several<ref name="ST" /> [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]<ref name="ST date">The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] had transitioned to become the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] by 4.3 ABY according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighters]] were in the midst of a [[Battle of Death Star III|battle]] with an Imperial [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] and its complement of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]]. Rex found his passenger craft caught in the Star Destroyer's [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]], but a tip from [[Red Leader (Star Tours)|one of the New Republic pilots]] to ease up on his main [[Engine/Legends|thruster]] allowed the droid to escape capture. The voyage nearly came to an end when an Imperial [[Starfighter/Legends|fighter]] shot the ship and caused it to lose altitude, but R2-D2 repaired the damaged [[Stabilizer/Legends|stabilizer]] on the Captain's orders. Rex then moved the starship to join the New Republic's [[Red Squadron (Star Tours)|Red Squadron]] in an attack run against a massive Imperial [[Death Star III|battlestation]]. After following two X-wings through a giant trench and helping them shoot down enemy TIE fighters, Rex and his passengers saw that the attack was a success. Rex then ordered R2-D2 to take the craft to lightspeed; they returned to the spaceport from which Flight ST-45 had originated, scathed but intact.<ref name="ST" />

RX-24's flight proved something of a harbinger for the future of the Star Tours travel agency. Within [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of the Battle of Endor,<ref name="G9" /> accidents and poor management drove the company to go out of business.<ref name="CSWE III 189b" />

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|Uh oh, wrong way&hellip; Brakes. Brakes. Where are the brakes?! Ahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh!|RX-24, on his maiden flight|<ref name="ST" />}}
[[File:RX-24.jpg|thumb|left|Rex mans the StarSpeeder 3000.]]
RX-24 was a standard RX-series model, making him a [[Class two droid/Legends|class two droid]],<ref name="ST" /><ref name="S&V" /> that is, one of a category of droids who aided in spaceflight and vehicle or starship maintenance. He possessed standard equipment for his model, including three clawed [[Limb/Legends|arms]] with which to manipulate starship controls, a [[Heuristic processor/Legends|heuristic processor]]<ref name="SGD" /> to facilitate learning and creativity,<ref name="SECR"> ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''</ref> two [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] with which to see,<ref name="SGD" /> a [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] platform at his base for locomotion, and a [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]] with which to speak.<ref name="ST" /><ref name="SGD" /> The droid was [[Programmer/Legends|programmed]] with a [[Gender/Legends|masculine]] personality,<ref name="ST" /> and he was able to speak and understand Basic and [[Binary/Legends|Binary]].<ref name="SGD" /> Rex's photoreceptors were [[Color/Legends|blue]]<ref name="Hasbro" /> unless illuminated, which made them shine with a white light.<ref name="ST" /> The wider sections of his chassis were burnished metal trimmed with gold and purple; between these were narrower sections in black. Rex's clawed fingers, upper anterior facial plating, and vocabulator were also gold. The droid pilot had a retractable purple visor that he could lower over his photoreceptors.<ref name="Hasbro" />

Upon his arrival at the Star Tours travel agency, RX-24 suffered from severe factory defects, sputtering random phrases and shorting out frequently.<ref name="ST2" /> Once restored to normal working order, Rex enjoyed the same programming as other RX units. He was skilled at starship piloting, ship maintenance, and [[Computer/Legends|computer]] use. His photoreceptors had great acuity to allow him to efficiently locate obstacles in spaceflight, and his dexterity enabled him to fly through dangerous situations.<ref name="SGD" /> Nevertheless, Rex had yet to become accustomed to actual spaceflight on his first mission; indeed, he exhibited some confusion and insecurity on the flight, nearly crashing the StarSpeeder 3000 and narrowly escaping several other hazards. Ultimately, his reflexes and daring allowed him to return to the Star Tours dock intact.<ref name="ST" />

Similarly, the fully functional Rex exhibited his model's ease of interaction with organic beings.<ref name="S&V" /> He was friendly and upbeat even in dire situations. When his first flight went awry, he tried to keep a professional veneer of calm, claiming that some of his mistakes had been intentional. Still, his anxieties manifested at particularly harrowing moments in screams and cries of exasperation. Despite his claims that he wanted to keep his passengers safe, RX-24 showed a daredevil streak on his maiden voyage; for instance, when he stumbled upon an Imperial battlestation, he chose to join a New Republic attack on it rather than retreat to safety. The pilot droid interacted smoothly with other mechanicals, such as his first navigator, R2-D2,<ref name="ST" /> as well as RX-24's romantic interest, ROX-N.<ref name="SWI104" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Conception===
{{Quote|Rex was a character we developed that tried to add some humor to the ride and, you know, I think it turned out really well.|George Lucas|<ref name="YT">{{YouTube|video=ErtzsMlIGgs|text=Star Wars George Lucas Interview by Tony Perri, Surf's Up Studios at Skywalker Ranch, Marin County|channel=@CoronadoBeachCompany|name=Coronado Beach Company est. 1886|date=2010-10-18}}</ref>}}
When [[Lucasfilm]] and [[the Walt Disney Company]] teamed up to create an attraction for the [[Disneyland]] theme park in [[Wikipedia:Anaheim, California|Anaheim, California]], the two sides chose to use flight simulator technology to allow the park guests to feel like they were traveling into space on a passenger liner. Creating the film to be projected to audience members proved a challenge, since all the drama had to come from either the visuals created by [[Industrial Light & Magic]] or from dialogue; the ride, therefore, needed a compelling and sympathetic narrator.<ref name="SWI104" />

[[George Lucas]] proposed a droid pilot for the role to help connect audience members to the greater experience the ride was intended to mimic.<ref name="SWI104" /> Lucas's original idea for the robot was to call him "Crazy Harry" and make him a sarcastic, wisecracking veteran of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="CoGL">''[[The Cinema of George Lucas]]''</ref> an idea based on the skippers of the [[Wikipedia:Jungle Cruise|Jungle Cruise]] attraction in the park's [[Wikipedia:Adventureland (Disney)|Adventureland]] area in the 1980s. However, the ride's director, [[Tony Baxter]], suggested the pilot be more of a jittery beginner and that the ride's harrowing narrative arise from the pilot's beginner's blunder; such a character would be more sympathetic, Baxter suggested. The team ran with the idea, also making the robot a stand-in for the audience members. For instance, the team felt that the pilot's insistence on participating in an attack run on a [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]]&mdash;along with his exclamation, "I've always wanted to do this!"&mdash;would mirror the feelings of anyone who had seen [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] [[Trench Run Defense|trench run]] in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="SWI104" />

===Development===
{{Quote|Finding the right voice for 'Rex' was a real challenge. As a first-time pilot, much of the adventure was going to be an out-of-control wild ride. That meant he was going to be doing a lot of screaming!|''Star Tours'' writer and producer Tom Fitzgerald|<ref name="SWI104" />}}
[[File:PaulReubens.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Comedian Paul Reubens provided the voice of RX-24.]]
The team then had to find a voice actor to perform the droid's lines. The idea that Rex had lost control of the StarSpeeder suggested the character would need to scream frequently on the audio track. [[Tom Fitzgerald]], lead writer and producer on the project,<ref name="SWI104" /> and [[Mark Eades]], media producer for the ride, have both claimed credit for eventually casting comedian [[Paul Reubens]] for the role.<ref name="OC Register">{{WebCite|url=http://ocresort.ocregister.com/2010/07/27/good-bye-star-tours-i-will-miss-you/51113|text=Good Bye Star Tours; I Will Miss You|author=Eades, Mark|date=2010-07-27|format=blog|work=The Orange County Register|archivedate=20100731083930}}</ref><ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.steelcitycollectibles.com//i/paul-reubens-rx-24-2018-topps-star-wars-stellar-signatures-autograph-green-19-20|text=Paul Reubens RX-24 2018 Topps Star Wars Stellar Signatures Autograph Green 19/20|work=Steel City Collectibles|archivedate=20230724150310}}</ref> Fitzgerald says that he thought Reubens might fit the bill after seeing the comedian's television special as the character [[Wikipedia:Pee-wee Herman|Pee-wee Herman]], a role that required Reubens to scream frequently and humorously. Fitzgerald felt the actor would fit the idea of a slightly comical, inexperienced pilot well.<ref name="SWI104" /> Eades's version of the story says that in seeking a voice actor who could portray a "slightly cracked' character, they auditioned over two dozen talents, including [[Wikipedia:Billy Barty|Billy Barty]] and [[Frank Welker]]. When Eades heard Reubens as the voice of a robot spaceship in the Disney film [[Wikipedia:Flight of the Navigator|''Flight of the Navigator'']], he thought the comedian would suit the part. Reubens soon signed on to the project.<ref name="OC Register" />

Lucas provided basic ideas for Rex's physical appearance. Based on these, [[Wikipedia:Walt Disney Imagineering|Imagineer]] [[Chris Runco]] sculpted a prototype Rex puppet from green foam. Two other ride designers, [[Larry Sheldon]] and [[Lance Updyke]], used this template to create the Rex puppets from aluminum. With four separate StarSpeeder 3000s that audience members might board in the attraction after its opening in [[1987]], four separate animatronic Rex puppets were also needed.<ref name="SWI104" /> The character first appeared in a [[1986]] [[George Lucas' Star Tours|TV promotion]] that aired on ABC's Sunday Night Movie feature, shortly before the ride officially opened at the start of the next year.<ref name="promo">[[George Lucas' Star Tours|George Lucas' ''Star Tours'']]</ref>

===Further developments===
[[File:StarToursEntrance96_wb.jpg|thumb|left|RX-24's flight is chronicled in the Star Tours attraction at various Disney amusement parks.]]
The ''Star Tours'' ride spread to other Disney parks, which required more Rex puppets to be created. With the opening of ''Star Tours'' at [[Disneyland Paris]], the designers added a new robot to the queue area of the attraction, ROX-N, whom they designed as Rex's girlfriend.<ref name="SWI104" /> Expansion to new parks meant finding new voice talents for non-English versions of the ride; for Disneyland Paris, the company cast voice actor [[Luq Hamet]] to portray Rex.<ref name="Disneyland Paris website">{{WebCite|url=http://www.disney77.fr/parc-disneyland/discoveryland/star-tour.html|text=Bienvenue dan l'univers magique de Disneyland Paris - les attractions de Disneyland Paris|format=website|work=Disney 77|archivedate=20170324152509}}</ref>

When Lucasfilm and Disney teamed up again to update ''Star Tours'' in [[2005]], designers decided to set the new version in the era between [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] and ''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'', well before the timeframe of the original ride. To preserve [[Canon|continuity]] with the original ride, wherein Rex tells guests that it is his first flight, the team decided to create a new pilot. The droid [[AC-38/Legends|AC-38]] ("Ace") was the result, and the new pilot exhibits similar physical and behavioral features to Rex. Nevertheless, the newer ride's plot sees the [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] C-3PO replace Ace by mistake. As a nod to the original ride, the designers included an RX-24 animatronic puppet in the queuing area audience members must pass through as they wait to board the attraction.<ref name="TIJ">{{InsiderCite|127|The Incredible Journey}}</ref> There, the pilot-to-be is non-functioning and marked defective, uttering lines from the original ''Star Tours'' seemingly at random.<ref name="ST2" /> ''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]'' opened to the public in [[2011]].<ref name="StarToursReturns">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/latestnews/story/Star_Tours_Returns_Starting_May_20th_136170.asp|text="Latest News - Star Tours Returns Starting May 20th"|author=Eric|date=2011-01-18|archivedate=20190729153331}}</ref>

===Continuity===
[[File:RX-24-fb.jpg|thumb|250px|RX-24]]
Sources disagree as to the manufacturer of the RX line of pilot droids. According to [[Scum and Villainy (sourcebook)|''Scum and Villainy'']] and ''[[Scavenger's Guide to Droids]]'', sourcebooks for the [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook|Saga Edition]] of the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' from [[Wizards of the Coast]] published in [[2008]] and [[2009]] respectively, RX-series pilot droids were produced by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] (IA).<ref name="S&V" /><ref name="SGD" /> However, RX-24's entry in 2008's ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' notes that he was manufactured by Reubens Robotic Systems.<ref name="CSWE III 117" /> This article assumes that despite the different manufacturer, as a factory-new droid, RX-24 still had all the standard features outlined in the roleplaying sourcebooks for IA's RX droids.

The short story "[[One Last Night in the Mos Eisley Cantina: The Tale of the Wolfman and the Lamproid]]," written by [[Judith Reeves-Stevens|Judith]] and [[Garfield Reeves-Stevens]] and published as part of ''[[Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina]]'' in [[1995]], includes a montage that sends the lovers [[Lak Sivrak/Legends|Lak Sivrak]] and [[Dice Ibegon/Legends|Dice Ibegon]] [[Time travel/Legends|skipping through time]]. At one point, they arrive at the Battle of Endor. As Alliance [[General/Legends|General]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] orders all fighters to attack the Death Star, Sivrak hears a droid exclaim that it "had always wanted to do this," mimicking Rex's line from ''Star Tours''. The story leaves the question of whether it is RX-24 unanswered, however.<ref name="OLNitMEC">{{StoryCite|story=One Last Night in the Mos Eisley Cantina: The Tale of the Wolfman and the Lamproid|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>
